name: Background Fetch
plain: Downloads large files after the person leaves, with a progress notification.
meaning: Lets a site download or upload big files outside the tab. The browser shows progress UI so the person can see and cancel it.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; Chrome shows a persistent progress notification the person can cancel.
steps: Call backgroundFetch.fetch with requests and downloadTotal
Worker handles success or failure events

limits.headline: Can download or upload big files after you leave the tab, with a progress notice
limits.user_action: You tap Download for a movie, podcast or large file and close the tab
can: Keep a large download or upload going after you leave the page
Show a progress notice that you can see and cancel
Finish the file and tell the site when it is done
cannot: Run silently, since Chrome shows a persistent progress notice
Keep going forever, since it stops when you cancel or the file finishes
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Chrome for Android only. Firefox, Safari and iPhone browsers do not support it.

story.what_it_is: A site can keep downloading a big file after you leave the page, and show progress in a notification.

marketing.name: Background Fetch
marketing.pitch: Lets web apps start large downloads that keep going even if you close the tab, with a progress notice.

story.for_you: You see a progress notification for a big download, like a movie or a game level. You can close the tab and it keeps going. When it finishes you get a note.
story.for_makers: Makers can offer offline movies, music and big game assets on the web, as native apps do. It keeps users from losing a half finished download. It uses the service worker, so it runs after the tab is gone.

use_cases.example: A web streaming app downloads a movie for a flight. You can close the tab while it finishes in the background.
A browser game downloads a large map pack after you leave the menu, and you get a notice when it is ready.
A web music player saves an album for offline listening while you do other things.
A learning site downloads a course video set for the commute.
A news reader site downloads the day's articles and images overnight for offline reading.
A web office app saves a large shared folder to the device for offline work.
A trip planner web app downloads offline maps and guides before you travel.
